title: SGLang Hits 928 tok/s on NVIDIA GB300 With Low Latency Mode
summary:
A new update to the SGLang framework enables faster text generation for AI agents on current generation hardware. By merging megakernel support in a new Low-Latency Mode, the project increased P90 per-user token speeds for the DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash model to 928 tok/s on NVIDIA GB300 and 516 tok/s on AMD MI355X GPUs. These gains, measured using DSpark in a SemiAnalysis AgentX trace replay, represent speed improvements of 1.38x for NVIDIA and 1.56x for AMD. The boost on NVIDIA chips comes from overlapping kernels that cut decoder layer time from 96.8 to 68.4 µs, while AMD results from merging multiple small kernels into two persistent kernels per layer.

The software was developed in collaboration with NVIDIA and AMD and is currently available through SGLang Docker images. Developers are now working on similar low-latency kernels for GLM-5.3, K3, and MiniMax M3 models. The team will provide additional details on the partnership at the SGLang Summit in San Francisco on Nov 12 and 13.

selectedTweets.text:
Introducing SGLang Low-Latency Mode, built with @NVIDIAAI and @AMD.

On DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with DSpark, it delivers up to 1.38× P90 per-user token speed on NVIDIA GB300 (671 to 928 tok/s) and 1.56× on AMD MI355X (332 to 516 tok/s) in @SemiAnalysis_'s AgentX trace replay.

Highlights:
- NVIDIA: overlapping kernels cut decoder layer time from 96.8 to 68.4 µs
- AMD: 2 persistent kernels per layer replace dozens of small ones, with cross-GPU communication overlapped inside them.
- New plugin system: custom kernels plug in from external libraries, with automatic fallback.
- Low-latency kernels for GLM-5.3, K3, and MiniMax M3 are in progress and will plug in next.
